questions.question: Rajagriha was the first capital of which Mahajanapada?
questions.solution:
Magadha was the first capital of the Magadha Mahajanapada before it was shifted to Pataliputra. Additional Info:
  • It was surrounded by five hills, making it virtually impregnable.
  • Bimbisara and Ajatashatru ruled from here.

questions.question: Which is the first garden - tomb in the Indian subcontinent?
questions.solution:
Humayun's Tomb in Delhi is the first garden-tomb in the Indian subcontinent. Key Facts:
  • Built by his widow, Bega Begum (Haji Begum).
  • It introduced the Persian Charbagh style to India.
  • It served as an architectural inspiration for the Taj Mahal.

questions.question: Baji Rao I or Baji Rao Ballal was the son of ________.
questions.solution:
Peshwa Balaji Vishwanath was the father of Baji Rao I. Baji Rao I is renowned for:
  • Expanding the Maratha Empire across North India.
  • Never losing a battle in his 20-year military career.
  • The victory at the Battle of Palkhed.

questions.question: Nalanda University, an important learning centre in ancient period is situated in which state?
questions.solution:
Bihar is the state where the ruins of the ancient Nalanda University are located. Exam Points:
  • Founded during the Gupta Empire (Kumaragupta I).
  • A world-renowned Buddhist center of learning.
  • Destroyed by Bakhtiyar Khilji in the late 12th century.

questions.question: Under the Delhi Sultanate, a religious tax ________ was imposed on the wealthy and rich Muslims in India.
questions.solution:
Zakat was the religious tax imposed on wealthy Muslims (usually 2.5% of savings). Other taxes:
  • Jizya: Tax on non-Muslim subjects.
  • Kharaj: Land tax.
  • Khums: One-fifth of the war booty.

questions.question: Who among the following founded the Widow Re-Marriage Association?
questions.solution:
Pandit Vishnu Shastri founded the Widow Re-Marriage Association in 1850. Context:
  • He was inspired by the social reform movements of the 19th century.
  • Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar was another pioneer who led to the Widow Remarriage Act of 1856.

questions.question: Which architectural style of India was distinguished by its use of hanging balconies and arch-shaped cornices?
questions.solution:
Rajput architecture is distinguished by hanging balconies (Jharokhas) and arch-shaped cornices. Features:
  • Intricate carvings and massive forts like Chittorgarh and Amer.
  • Use of Chhatris (dome-shaped pavilions).

questions.question: Who among the following was the last Pallava king?
questions.solution:
Aparajitavarman was the last ruler of the Pallava dynasty. History:
  • The Pallavas were defeated by Aditya Chola I in the late 9th century.
  • They are famous for the Shore Temple at Mahabalipuram.

questions.question: Who was the Governor-General of India when Doctrine of Lapse was introduced in India?
questions.solution:
Lord Dalhousie introduced the Doctrine of Lapse. Impact:
  • States like Satara, Jaitpur, Sambalpur, and Jhansi were annexed if a ruler died without a natural heir.
  • This was a major cause of the Revolt of 1857.

questions.question: Who among the following was the Governor-General from 1773 to 1785?
questions.solution:
Warren Hastings served as the Governor-General from 1773 to 1785. Achievements:
  • First Governor-General of Bengal under the Regulating Act of 1773.
  • Established the dual system of administration abolition and founded the Asiatic Society of Bengal with William Jones.

questions.question: The Ilbert Bill was passed during the term of Lord Ripon to bring Indian and European magistracy on equal footing in ________.
questions.solution:
1883 was the year the Ilbert Bill was introduced during Lord Ripon's tenure. Significance:
  • Aimed to allow Indian judges to try Europeans.
  • Met with fierce opposition from the British community, leading to a compromise.

questions.question: Subsidiary Alliance was a system devised by_________ in 1798
questions.solution:
Lord Wellesley devised the Subsidiary Alliance in 1798. Features:
  • Indian rulers had to maintain British troops and keep a British Resident.
  • Hyderabad was the first state to accept it.

questions.question: Lord William Bentinck with the support of Raja Rammohan Roy abolished the practice of_________.
questions.solution:
Sati was abolished in 1829 by Lord William Bentinck. Details:
  • Raja Rammohan Roy played a crucial role in campaigning against this practice.
  • It was declared illegal and punishable by criminal courts via Regulation XVII.

questions.question: Who gave title of “Father of the Nation” to Mahatma Gandhi?
questions.solution: Subhas Chandra Bose first addressed Mahatma Gandhi as the 'Father of the Nation' in a radio address from Singapore in 1944. Note: Rabindranath Tagore gave him the title 'Mahatma'.

questions.question: Mahatma Gandhi called off the Non — cooperation Movement in February 1922 after which incident?
questions.solution:
Chauri Chaura Incident (Feb 1922) led Gandhi to call off the Non-Cooperation Movement. Details:
  • A violent mob burnt a police station killing 22 policemen.
  • Gandhi emphasized that the movement must remain strictly non-violent.

questions.question: In pre-independent India, who was the first person to discuss the concept of poverty line?
questions.solution: Dadabhai Naoroji was the first to discuss the poverty line in his book 'Poverty and Un-British Rule in India'. Key Term: Drain of Wealth theory.

questions.question: Which freedom fighter of India led the famous revolt of 1857 (sepoy mutiny) at Lucknow?
questions.solution:
Begum Hazrat Mahal led the 1857 revolt in Lucknow. Context:
  • She was the wife of the exiled Nawab of Awadh, Wajid Ali Shah.
  • She declared her son, Birjis Qadr, as the ruler.

questions.question: In a drama, Hema spoke “Swaraj is my birth right and I shall have it”. Which Indian freedom fighter gave this slogan?
questions.solution: Lokmanya Bal Gangadhar Tilak gave the slogan 'Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it!'. Info: Known as the 'Father of Indian Unrest' and founder of the Home Rule League.

questions.question: During which freedom struggle movement, Mahatma Gandhi Ji gave the call for "Do or Die"?
questions.solution: Quit India movement (1942) is when Gandhi gave the 'Do or Die' call. Other name: August Kranti. It demanded an immediate end to British rule in India.

questions.question: Which freedom fighter was also the first woman to become the Governor of Uttar Pradesh State?
questions.solution:
Sarojini Naidu was the first woman Governor of an Indian state (Uttar Pradesh). Achievements:
  • Known as the 'Nightingale of India'.
  • First Indian woman President of the Indian National Congress (1925).

questions.question: When was the Gandhi-Irwin pact signed?
questions.solution:
1931 was the year the Gandhi-Irwin Pact was signed. Outcome:
  • INC agreed to join the Second Round Table Conference.
  • British agreed to release political prisoners.

questions.question: Who was the founder of a non-violent movement named as “Khudai Khidmatgars”?
questions.solution: Khan Abdul Ghaffar Khan (Frontier Gandhi) founded the Khudai Khidmatgars. Known as: The 'Red Shirts'. They were a non-violent group in the North-West Frontier Province.

questions.question: Which freedom fighter was involved in the Kakori Train Action in 1925, for which the British government condemned him to death?
questions.solution: Ram Prasad Bismil was a key figure in the 1925 Kakori Train Action. Revolutionaries involved: Ashfaqulla Khan, Thakur Roshan Singh, and Rajendra Lahiri (all were executed).

questions.question: Jyotiba Phule founded which of the following organizations?
questions.solution: Satyashodhak Samaj (Truth Seekers' Society) was founded by Jyotiba Phule in 1873. Goal: To liberate the shudra and untouchable castes from exploitation and promote education.

questions.question: The split in Indian National Congress occured in _________.
questions.solution: 1907 is the year of the Surat Split. Details: The Congress split into two factions: Moderates (led by Gokhale) and Extremists (led by Tilak).
